A.question: Can private_audit_cli return 0 with one fully reviewed manifest while a second raw object remains unreferenced after an earlier manifest write failure?
A.acceptance: Aggregate-only read-only auditor counts unreferenced digest-name files and transient/unexpected private object entries, avoiding raw paths/content; CLI returns 2 if orphan/unsafe entries exist; add synthetic tests for orphan and clean capture.

hypotheses: No orphan detection currently; manifest-backed checks can be clean when an unindexed object remains
A bounded dirfd listing can detect orphan object names without viewing original content
Scanning can race active writes; any uncertainty must fail closed without a release claim

C.plan: Inspect object hierarchy; use fdesc-only listing of objects and two-character shards with validated names, compare against valid declared manifest SHA paths, bounded count; never follow links or mutate. Add test with two fake objects and manifest only for one; CLI exit2.

D.falsifier: CLI returns 0 with orphan, newly created missing directories during read, raw path leaks to CLI output.
D.scope: Only local POSIX store, no release right and no user personal data
